key_insight: This paper shows that spiking neural networks can be made much more efficient when the model and chip are designed together. By using a dual memory pathway, the system achieves over 4× higher throughput and about 5× better energy efficiency while also needing 40–60% fewer parameters.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic AI systems often face a trade-off between performance, energy efficiency, and model size. This work addresses how to build spiking networks that are both hardware-friendly and competitive in efficiency without requiring large parameter counts.
method: Designs a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to better match neuromorphic computation.
Co-optimizes the network architecture with a custom neuromorphic chip for efficient execution.
Reduces parameter count while improving throughput and energy efficiency compared with state-of-the-art implementations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical path toward faster and more energy-efficient edge or embedded AI using neuromorphic hardware. It also highlights the value of algorithm–hardware co-design as a way to improve real-world deployment efficiency, not just model accuracy.
visual_elements: A side-by-side diagram of the dual memory pathway architecture versus a standard spiking network

paper_title: Algorithm–hardware co-design of neuromorphic networks with dual memory pathways
paper_authors: Pengfei Sun, Zhe Su, Jascha Achterberg, Giacomo Indiveri, Dan F. M. Goodman
